topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the primary learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Intrinsic and environmental factors in cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relative contributions of intrinsic biological processes, bad luck, and environmental exposures to cancer development through genetic and epidemiological perspectives.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how pathogens and oncogenic viruses contribute to carcinogenesis, focusing on the cooperative mechanism in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical agents, directly or through metabolic activation, cause DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanistic integration
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the non-mutagenic drivers of cancer, including tumor promoters, host developmental susceptibility, and how they integrate with mutagens to enable malignancy.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and evaluating carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity and evaluate exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the final concluding remarks and summary points for the lecture.
